A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ShapeShifter and contain readable main text and supplementary material. Their methods, equations, experiments, tables and figures can be matched reliably across wording and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ShapeShifter generation experiments, quality and diversity scores, runtime measurements and ablations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments, runtime measurements, generated examples and ablations in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The sparse voxel representation, point/normal/color features, learned upsamplers, diffusion objectives, pruning and meshing procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight main benchmark exemplars and retain the open-surface, editing, texturing and supplementary examples. The untextured vase and pig experiments already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Sin3DM and Sin3DGen remain the main comparators; SSG remains in the timing and supplementary quantitative comparisons, and Rodin remains in Figure 10. The new Xcube discussion introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Training iterations, model configurations, preprocessing, SSFID and diversity metrics, evaluation resolutions and ten-variant sampling remain unchanged. The supplementary batch-one DDIM timing protocol is also retained. Revised runtime wording does not establish a changed training procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the learned-upsampling, SDF-feature, QEM-averaging and color-removal ablations, together with the same editing and open-surface demonstrations. Cropping and enlarging existing illustrations adds no analysis.

E5.justification: The reporting practice is unchanged: both provide point estimates and the same ten-variant diversity calculation, without adding independent-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported training-time scope: v1 says the five-level hierarchy trains in 12 minutes, whereas v2 says each level trains in 12 minutes. All entries in Tables 1–4 remain identical, including Table 2's unqualified 12-minute entry. This is a limited revision to a reported timing result, without evidence of rerunning experiments or a measurable aggregate runtime change.

T1.justification: The feature definition, diffusion formulation and losses in Equations 1–4 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, proofs or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: detailed single-exemplar shape generation, efficient sparse multiscale processing, interactive control and support for closed and open surfaces.

C2.justification: Section 2 adds an applicability argument that Xcube's pretrained VAEs and SDF representation are not adapted to single-shape variations. ShapeShifter's own limitations, interpretations of its ablations, and supplementary cautions about metrics and Sin3DM preprocessing remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 replaces the promise to release code upon acceptance with reported code availability and a project-page hyperlink. Section 5.1 also identifies the 12-minute training time as per level. Software, hardware and hyperparameter disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges the already-cited Xcube's earlier efficient multiscale diffusion pipeline and distinguishes ShapeShifter's single-exemplar setting. The same 123 referenced works remain; other bibliography changes concern formatting and metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and grammar edits, updates an affiliation, standardizes bibliography presentation and adds acknowledgments. Supplementary sections are consequently renumbered, while the scientific narrative and section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays are rearranged, including Figures 4 and 9 and supplementary Table 4. Figure 8's panels are cropped, and Figure 14 enlarges the existing vase and pig examples. No scientific figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The project-page link and reported code availability provide more actionable reproducibility guidance than v1's future-release promise. Clearer positioning against Xcube and enlarged supplementary examples also help readers assess the work. These are modest documentation and presentation gains; the experimental evidence is unchanged. The improvement is qualified by the revised per-level training-time statement, which remains unreconciled with Table 2 and Section 2's claim of under 12 minutes for the entire process.
